items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: >> [(note)] Butch was interviewed at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party in Scottsdale, Arizona on March 4, 1995 by Dr. Michael Woods and Monk Rowe.

ctx.x: Charles “Butch” Miles is a well known figure on the national and international jazz scene. Born on July 4, 1944, he grew up in Charlestown, West Virginia. He took to the drums early on and became one of the youngest drummers to ever drive the Count Basie band. Butch has supported such stellar artists as Tony Bennett, Joe Williams, Lena Horne, Dave Brubeck and Frank Sinatra. His travels have taken him from South America to the Far East and his motion picture credits include “The Last of the Blue Devils” with Count…
Butch was interviewed at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party in Scottsdale, Arizona on March 4, 1995 by Dr. Michael Woods and Monk Rowe.

We are here as part of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and we have with us one of the finest drummers in the country, Butch Miles. We just finished a burning set with the Paradise Valley Jazz Party musicians, and welcome.

ctx.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive at Hamilton College and I’m very pleased to have a re-visit with drummer Butch Miles. Thanks for joining me today.
I’m very happy to be here, Monk, thank you for asking me.
